integer_bounds.description: Wire 1.1: every int is a JSON number from 0 to 2^53 - 1 (9007199254740991), without sign, fraction or exponent. Each case is the operation named in based_on with its orphan_after written as number, signed again by its writer, so its signature verifies and only the integer rule decides: the largest integer is valid; 2^53, a fraction (86400.0 included), an exponent and a sign are refused with 400 bad_request, before the operation's fields are read. Only the opaque members wire 1.1 names by path are exempt: a message body's metadata and a tasks.done body's proof (encoding.json json).

permanent_policies.description: Wire 6.2, spec 10.3.1: a record.put at a permanent policy. cases are the record.put create of operations at its policy made permanent, its permanent member written after write_scopes as { "generation": g }, naming no generation and naming generation 1, the account's: each key derived again for its policy (wire 1.5), its value sealed again for that key, each a batch of its own, signed again by the wallet, which the service takes. rejections are the case naming generation 1 with its permanent member written as permanent gives, signed again by the wallet, so its signature verifies and only the member's form refuses it, 400 bad_request, as the operation is read: generation is required, an int (wire 1.1) or null, and the only member, and permanent is an object.

shape_rejections.description: Wire 6.2, 6.4 step 9: operations whose shape the service refuses, 400 bad_request, before it compares them with what it holds. Each case is the operation of operations named in based_on with the change its name gives made in its signed body, its record key derived again for the policy it then has (wire 1.5), and signed again by its writer, so its signature verifies and only the shape decides. A record's read_scope, its value_sealed's scope with it, and each write_scopes entry follow the scope rule of wire 3.1 "Scope names"; a key_bundle.put's range starts at data epoch 1 and its first_epoch is at most its last_epoch (wire 3.5, 6.2); a record.put at a permanent policy, its permanent member written after write_scopes, deletes only in a generation above the one the policy names, never when it names none, and creates only in the generation it names (wire 6.2 "Permanent policies", spec 10.3.1).

batch_entries.description: Wire 1.1, 2.2, 6.4: an entry of a POST /ops body has only its own members: a signed operation's carrying form body and sig, a cursor.set its op and position. unknown_members.description: Wire 1.1, 6.1: unknown members are refused at every depth of an operation body, as at its top level: in batch, a condition and its object, expected_version, value_sealed, id_inputs, the carrying form of a signed record or cert, and the key bundle. Each case is the operation named in based_on with the member future_restriction added at the path in member (a dotted path; numbers index arrays), signed again by its writer, so its signature verifies and only the member check refuses it: 400 bad_request.
